html:
The Tupari are an Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, living near the Branco River, a tributary of the Guaporé. Their language is one of the six Tupari languages of the Tupian family, and is spoken by only a few hundred people.

They farm manioc and maize in forest gardens, hunt and fish, and are known for their shamans and their beer feasts. Neighbours include the Makurap and the Sakurabiat.

Rubber tappers reached their land in the early 1900s, after the Amazon rubber boom, and brought epidemics that killed most of the Tupari. The survivors now live with other peoples in the Rio Branco and Guaporé indigenous lands of Brazil.
